92.$description: white at .92. secondary text (D-012: .85 measured 3.3-3.79:1 on the book over sunlit photos)

kiln.why.why: white at fixed opacities makes glass, rims, rings and dividers, so each one reads as light on top of the scene and the scene stays visible under it

850.$description: sunken well (code) on a solid dark page

900.$description: raised panel on a solid dark page

950.$description: page background for solid (non-glass) screens, dark theme

kiln.why.why: one neutral ramp from near-white to near-black, slightly cool so it sits with the ink, for opaque reading surfaces, the reduced-transparency fallback and diagrams; steps light to dark so neighbours read apart

700.$description: the lit top of the ink solid in the light theme (R-010)

950.$description: the studio's ground in dark: deep enough that a level-1 pane steps at least 1.15:1 off it (G-EL1; #111214 gave 1.09, #0A0A0C 1.13)

kiln.why.why: one near-black for text on white fills and on light glass, slightly warm so it sits with photographs instead of looking printed

400.$description: blue bright enough to read as a small mark on dark glass

800.$description: the foot of the accent sheet, where its own shade falls (R-010)

kiln.why.why: the one promoted-action colour; 600 carries white text at 4.70:1 and 700 is its hover, darker so the pressed-in feeling matches the lift
black at fixed opacities for scrims and halos, used where a photo under text needs darkening by a measured amount
placeholder art for covers before a real image loads, taken from the anchor scene so the empty state still looks like a place

400.$description: green bright enough to read as a small mark on dark glass

kiln.why.why: status colour for success; carries white text at 5.02:1 so the meaning is readable as text as well as colour

700.$description: amber dark enough to read as a small mark on light glass

kiln.why.why: status colour for warnings; bright enough to be seen on glass and paired with ink text at 9.90:1

400.$description: red bright enough to read as a small mark on dark glass

kiln.why.why: status colour for errors and destructive actions; carries white text at 5.66:1
ink at fixed opacities builds the light theme the same way white builds the dark one, with rings, dividers and secondary text over a lifted scene

0.$description: page background for solid screens, light theme

50.$description: opaque fallback surface in the light theme

100.$description: sunken well (code) on a solid light page

150.$description: the shaded foot of the white loud solid, lit from above (R-012)

kiln.why.why: opaque near-whites for light reading surfaces and the light-theme fallback, a step apart so page, raised and sunken stay distinguishable
the system owns no hue of its own because the scene behind the glass supplies the hue; white is the base every translucent layer is made of
the accent blue at low opacity, the only tint a plain field is allowed, so a field stays almost colourless and the scene keeps the colour
the bright accent blue at a fixed opacity, the one colour a diagram may use, strong enough to separate a part from the dark ground at 3:1

1.$description: level 1, a pane: smoked body at 78%

2.$description: level 2, a surface nested in a pane: +7% white, no second blur

3.$description: level 3, an overlay such as a dialog: 92%

scrim.$description: under an overlay, the scene and panes dim to half

kiln.why.why: smoked glass bodies for each level of the stack, a measured step apart so a pane, a surface inside it, an overlay and a popover read as four layers (R-013)

glass.$description: the dark glass body at 45%: thin enough that the scene shows through as glass, with the dimming doing the work of legibility (D-035); the 78% smoke.1 read as an opaque slab

glass-light.$description: the light glass body at 66%: the scene shows through as frosted glass while ink keeps its contrast (D-035)

kiln.why.why: the loud solid is a warm off-white, lit at its top, so it reads as lit glass rather than a white hole
a chosen item is a lighter pane of grey glass in dark and white in light, resting in its track

base.$description: aurora mesh: the pale ground the colour pools sit in

peach.$description: aurora mesh: warm pool, top left

coral.$description: aurora mesh: coral pool, top right

lilac.$description: aurora mesh: lilac pool, bottom left

kiln.why.why: data colours belong to the content a chart shows, like a scene or a photo; the interface around the chart still owns no hue (D-031)

light-1.$description: data slot 1, blue, stepped for the light surface; order is the CVD-safety mechanism (validated adjacent pairs)

dark-1.$description: data slot 1, blue, stepped for the dark surface; same hue as light-1

light-2.$description: data slot 2, orange, stepped for the light surface; order is the CVD-safety mechanism (validated adjacent pairs)

dark-2.$description: data slot 2, orange, stepped for the dark surface; same hue as light-2

light-3.$description: data slot 3, aqua, stepped for the light surface; order is the CVD-safety mechanism (validated adjacent pairs)

dark-3.$description: data slot 3, aqua, stepped for the dark surface; same hue as light-3

light-4.$description: data slot 4, yellow, stepped for the light surface; order is the CVD-safety mechanism (validated adjacent pairs)

dark-4.$description: data slot 4, yellow, stepped for the dark surface; same hue as light-4

light-5.$description: data slot 5, magenta, stepped for the light surface; order is the CVD-safety mechanism (validated adjacent pairs)

dark-5.$description: data slot 5, magenta, stepped for the dark surface; same hue as light-5

light-6.$description: data slot 6, green, stepped for the light surface; order is the CVD-safety mechanism (validated adjacent pairs)

dark-6.$description: data slot 6, green, stepped for the dark surface; same hue as light-6

light-7.$description: data slot 7, violet, stepped for the light surface; order is the CVD-safety mechanism (validated adjacent pairs)

dark-7.$description: data slot 7, violet, stepped for the dark surface; same hue as light-7

light-8.$description: data slot 8, red, stepped for the light surface; order is the CVD-safety mechanism (validated adjacent pairs)

dark-8.$description: data slot 8, red, stepped for the dark surface; same hue as light-8

seq-dark-1.$description: sequential step 1 of 5 for the dark surface: more is brighter

seq-light-1.$description: sequential step 1 of 5 for the light surface: more is deeper

seq-dark-2.$description: sequential step 2 of 5 for the dark surface: more is brighter

seq-light-2.$description: sequential step 2 of 5 for the light surface: more is deeper

seq-dark-3.$description: sequential step 3 of 5 for the dark surface: more is brighter

seq-light-3.$description: sequential step 3 of 5 for the light surface: more is deeper

seq-dark-4.$description: sequential step 4 of 5 for the dark surface: more is brighter

seq-light-4.$description: sequential step 4 of 5 for the light surface: more is deeper

seq-dark-5.$description: sequential step 5 of 5 for the dark surface: more is brighter

seq-light-5.$description: sequential step 5 of 5 for the light surface: more is deeper

kiln.why.why: 64px is the blur where small bright spots in the photos average out enough for text to pass; 20px is for small scrims that must keep detail

mesh.$description: melts the mesh's pools into each other: wide enough that no pool keeps an edge

clear.$description: the glass blur for D-035: soft enough that text never sits on a hard edge, clear enough that the scene keeps its shapes, so glass reads as glass and not as a tinted slab

kiln.why.why: glass slightly boosts the colour it shows so the dimmed scene still reads as the same place in its own colours
a 4px grid with a few half steps; every gap in the system is a multiple so related things align and the padding inside a pane can always exceed the gap between its items

control-xl.$description: a control the hand holds as a whole bar, such as a fill slider: 56px

measure.$description: about 70 characters per line in proportional type (the ch unit is the width of "0", wider than the average letter, so 64ch ran to 85+ characters)

touch.$description: minimum touch target (WCAG 2.5.8 asks 24px; Apple HIG 44pt)

menu-min.$description: narrowest a dropdown list may be

slider-min.$description: the shortest a slider may get: enough travel to set a value by feel, and a width that does not follow its value text

kiln.why.why: fixed physical sizes for hairlines and rings that stay crisp, a 44px touch size, and avatar and icon sizes that keep the anchor proportions

kbd.$description: a keycap: the height of a caption line with a little room

overlay-md.$description: a dialog's width: a comfortable measure for a question and its answer

overlay-lg.$description: a wide dialog or a bottom sheet on a tablet: a short form fits

overlay-side.$description: a side drawer: the width of a phone, for navigation and filters

overlay-pop.$description: a popover: wide enough for a sentence and two controls

overlay-tip.$description: a tooltip: a few words, never a paragraph

overlay-toast.$description: the toast column at the top end

grabber.$description: the grabber on a bottom sheet: wide enough to find with a thumb

fab.$description: a floating action button: a step larger than an IconButton, at thumb reach

listbox-max.$description: a popup list stops at about seven rows and scrolls, so it never covers the page

input-min.$description: the text part of a field that holds chips never gets narrower than a short word

radio-card-min.$description: a radio card is never narrower than a short title and a line of detail

star.$description: a rating star: big enough to read the score at a glance

nav-bar.$description: a top bar: a 44px row with room above and below

nav-item.$description: a bottom-nav destination: icon and label stacked

nav-item-min.$description: the narrowest a bottom-nav destination gets

nav-panel.$description: a navigation panel: a column of links with a line each

segment-min.$description: the narrowest segment of a segmented control

scale-label.$description: the label column of a Scale row: room for a two-word axis name, the same in every row so tracks line up

scale-word.$description: the word column of a Scale row, the width of a short level word

kiln.why.why: corners nest, so the 40px pane minus its 22px inset padding gives the 18px media corner, minus 16px gives the 24px inner surface, and controls are full pills because they are held

sans.$value: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Display', 'SF Pro Text', Inter, system-ui, sans-serif

kiln.why.why: the platform system face, the same one visionOS uses, so the glass reads as part of the device rather than a website on top of it

450.$description: long-form reading size (docs prose, articles); Carbon body-long and Material body-large are 16px

kiln.why.why: a short scale with one size per role, 11 to 17 for interface text, 16 for long reading and 21 to 44 for titles
three weights only, so the semibold of the one loud action and the title keeps meaning something

long.$description: line height for long-form reading at 16px

kiln.why.why: tight for titles and controls, 1.42 for short interface text, 1.6 for long reading where the eye must find the next line
small caps labels need extra space to stay legible at 11px, and large titles need a little less to hold together as one word shape

halo.$description: legibility halo for white text on thin glass (WCAG 1.4.3 Understanding: text with a halo)

kiln.why.why: shadows sit below a pane to say how far it floats; the halo is the measured text halo that WCAG allows on thin glass, with lighter variants for the light theme

well.$description: a recessed track holding its choices

cast.$description: a solid control resting on a pane: a tight contact shadow and a soft one below

cast-press.$description: pushed back toward the pane, the soft shadow tightens

cast-accent.$description: the accent sheet lets blue light fall on the pane under it

bead.$description: a switch knob is a bead sitting in its recess

carve.$description: a recess cut into glass: shade under the top lip, light on the bottom lip, a faint edge

groove.$description: a field is a groove in the glass: shade under its top lip, a faint light on its bottom lip, and an edge all round that carries the 3:1 boundary

lens.$description: a highlighted menu row is a lens of glass with light on its top edge

etch.$description: a label etched into glass: shade under its top edge, light along its bottom edge

portrait.$description: a portrait behind a lens: a rim of light, brightest at the top, and shade at the foot

track.$description: a track is a shallow recess: light from above leaves a shade under its top edge

loud-glow.$description: the promoted solid glows with its own light onto the pane

quiet-cast.$description: a quiet glass object resting on the pane

chosen-cast.$description: a chosen pane resting in its track

on-glow.$description: a switch that is on is lit, and its light spills a little onto the pane

level-1.$description: a pane floats well off the scene

level-2.$description: a nested surface rests on its pane

level-3.$description: an overlay floats highest, over a dimmed scene

edge.$description: a slab of glass: a faint edge all round and shade gathering at its foot

bloom.$description: the loud solid blooms with its own light

glow-soft.$description: emitted light around a lit value or a powered part in dark: centred, no offset, back to the ground within ~3× its blur

glow-soft-light.$description: light theme: nothing emits; the same part reads by its solid ink

glow-mark.$description: emitted light around a small mark that says now (a current-step dot, a value marker); relatively wider because the mark is small

ring.$description: the groove ring alone: a hairline all round that carries a 3:1 boundary on dark glass

ring-light.$description: the light-theme groove ring alone: an ink hairline all round that carries a 3:1 boundary on pale glass

kiln.why.why: 200ms for a reply to a press, 420ms for hover and small changes, 640ms for arriving and scene changes, so motion settles instead of snapping

spin.$description: one turn of a spinner: steady, not frantic

breathe.$description: half a breath of a skeleton: slow enough to read as waiting, not flashing

soft.$description: long, soft settle. no snap, no overshoot

kiln.why.why: a long ease-out that lands softly for things arriving or responding, and a symmetric curve for crossfades where nothing arrives

dim.$description: Uncalibrated and held at the bright value

mid.$description: Uncalibrated and held at the bright value

bright.$description: D-035: 0.48 for bright scenes. Earlier note, 0.42: thinnest glass where the whole book stays >=3.8:1 on every photo (0.44 left 6 City nodes at 3.56-3.79); 0.38 passes every node at 4.5:1; between 3.8 and 4.5 = E-001

light.$description: light theme lifts the backdrop instead of dimming it

kiln.why.why: how much glass dims or lifts the scene; 0.42 is the thinnest value that keeps every measured node above the exception floor on all four photos, 1.12 lifts for the light theme
movement is small, a 2px lift on hover and a 16px rise on entry, so the layout never appears to shift
a pressed control shrinks to 97 percent, enough to feel pushed without changing its layout
widths where the layout changes column count, chosen at common phone, tablet and laptop edges so content reflows instead of zooming
maximum content widths, so reading lines and grids stop growing on very wide screens
4, 8 and 12 columns, each divisible into halves and thirds, so panes can share a row at every breakpoint
a few named layers in order (content, raised, sticky, overlay, toast) so a pane never ends up behind something it should float above
one fixed half opacity, so every disabled control fades by the same amount and reads as the same state everywhere

ambient.$description: how strongly a mesh object lights what is under it

dim.$description: how far a skeleton fades at the bottom of its breath

wash.$description: the wash under a single line series, a tint that never reads as a solid block

kiln.why.why: the raw proportions behind the named aspect ratios, one place to change a shape

sheet-max.$description: a bottom sheet stops short of the top so the screen behind still shows
